summary: OSCAR translates user instructions into Python control code while observing screen images and acting through mouse and keyboard operations. A state-machine controller handles errors and replans tasks during execution across desktop and mobile applications.

name: AutoDroid-V2: Boosting SLM-based GUI Agents via Code Generation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a visual IDE environment and benchmark for software-engineering tasks, comparing screenshot-based control with access to editing and shell tools.

summary: Introduces a modular visual web-agent stack with planning and memory components, exposed through a remote-browser application and Chrome extension.

name: API Agents vs. GUI Agents: Divergence and Convergence
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Compares API-driven and GUI-driven agents across architecture, development, and interaction considerations, discussing when hybrid approaches are useful.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SkillWeaver explores websites, practices interactions, and converts the resulting experience into a reusable library of callable skill APIs. Its WebArena and live-website experiments examine skill refinement, composition, and transfer from stronger agents to weaker ones.

name: LiteCUA: Computer as MCP Server for Computer-Use Agent on AIOS
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AIOS 1.0 exposes computer states and actions through an MCP server to provide structured environmental context for agents. LiteCUA is a lightweight agent built on this interface, evaluated on OSWorld to study the effect of computer-environment contextualization.

name: MCPWorld: A Unified Benchmarking Testbed for API, GUI, and Hybrid Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced. The platform or GUI evaluation setting was additionally checked in the primary full text.
summary: MCPWorld evaluates API, GUI, and hybrid computer-use agents with 201 tasks in applications whose source can be instrumented and extended with MCP support. It verifies completion from application behavior and packages the testbed in containers with GPU support.

name: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Magentic-UI combines browser interaction, code execution, file operations, and MCP tools in an interface for human-agent collaboration. It studies collaborative planning and task execution, action guards, and persistent memory through benchmark tasks, simulated users, user studies, and safety assessments.

name: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-Agent System with Coding Actions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.

name: ComputerRL: Scaling End-to-End Online Reinforcement Learning for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Combines API and GUI actions with distributed desktop reinforcement learning and alternating supervised training to address training instability.

name: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.

name: MAS-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Shortcut-Augmented Hybrid Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MAS-Bench evaluates mobile agents that combine GUI actions with APIs, deep links, and reusable scripts. Its 139 tasks across 11 apps test use of 88 predefined shortcuts as well as the ability to generate new reusable workflows.

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.

name: WALT: Web Agents that Learn Tools
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

name: \textsc{GUI-Spotlight}: Adaptive Iterative Focus Refinement for Enhanced GUI Visual Grounding
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.

name: UltraCUA: A Foundation Model for Computer Use Agents with Hybrid Action
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UltraCUA trains a shared policy for primitive GUI actions and high-level tool calls using synthesized tasks and hybrid trajectories. Supervised fine-tuning followed by online reinforcement learning is evaluated on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.

name: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OSWorld-MCP evaluates how agents choose between GUI operations and MCP tool calls in computer tasks. It combines generated and curated tools, with 158 manually validated tools across seven applications, to examine tool use alongside task completion.

name: Step-GUI Technical Report
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. The report also introduces GUI-MCP for hierarchical GUI operations and local task delegation, and AndroidDaily for static-action and end-to-end mobile evaluation.

name: MobileWorld: Benchmarking Autonomous Mobile Agents in Agent-User Interactive and MCP-Augmented Environments
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces long mobile workflows that combine agent-user interaction, cross-application tasks, and MCP-based tool access.

name: MAI-UI Technical Report: Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: MAI-UI combines GUI navigation, native user interaction, and MCP tool calls in a family of policies trained through generated data and online reinforcement learning. The report also studies device-cloud routing and scaling of parallel environments and interaction budgets, with grounding and Android navigation evaluation.

name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.

name: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CUA-Skill encodes Windows application knowledge in parameterized skills and execution/composition graphs. Its agent retrieves and instantiates these skills and uses memory for failure recovery, with end-to-end evaluation on WindowsAgentArena.

name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.

name: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ToolTok represents GUI operations with learned tool tokens and frames interaction as progressive tool selection. Semantic anchoring and an easy-to-hard curriculum teach tool meanings before visual pathfinding, with evaluation across grounding scenarios.

name: Mobile-Agent-v3.5: Multi-platform Fundamental GUI Agents
notes: Summary and topic tags reviewed against the primary abstract. Reported experiments, task counts, and artifact availability are not independently reproduced.
summary: Presents GUI-Owl-1.5 variants and a hybrid data pipeline for multimodal GUI interaction, tool use, memory, and multi-platform tasks.

name: WeaveBench: A Long-Horizon, Real-World Benchmark for Computer-Use Agents with Hybrid Interfaces
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: WeaveBench requires agents to combine GUI, command-line and code operations within long tasks on an Ubuntu desktop. A trajectory-aware judge checks deliverables and interaction evidence, including shortcut behavior that outcome-only grading can miss.

name: ComAct: Reframing Professional Software Manipulation via COM-as-Action Paradigm
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: ComAct proposes COM program synthesis as an alternative interface for manipulating professional software and introduces ComCADBench with GUI-based comparison agents. ComActor adds a staged training and correction approach, supported by a Windows-container training platform.

name: Beyond the GUI Paradigm: Do Mobile Agents Need the Phone Screen?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: This study compares general coding agents using mobile command-line access with reproducible GUI agents on AndroidWorld and MobileWorld. It also supplies oracle CLI analyses and a separate task suite for operations such as bulk changes, filtering and hidden device state.

name: MacAgentBench: Benchmarking AI Agents on Real-World macOS Desktop
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces macOS tasks spanning GUI and command-line interaction, with deterministic checks and intermediate-progress scoring for application workflows.

name: StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces StateAct, a code-first computer-use harness that manipulates program state directly and delegates screenshot-and-click subgoals to a GUI agent. An independent completion gate checks saved outputs, while fresh subagents handle subgoals to limit accumulated context.

name: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces an Interactive Reward Agent that proposes completion conditions and verifies them using system, application, and GUI tools after execution. GUI-RewardBench provides annotated desktop trajectories for evaluating these evidence-based judgments and their use in reinforcement learning.

name: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Describes a foundation GUI agent with combined GUI and command-line actions, large-scale interaction infrastructure, and iterative environment and task generation.

name: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Proposes WebMCP-Phalanx, a browser-integrated runtime that binds page-exposed tools to their registering principals and separates content inspection from privileged invocation. It studies lifecycle and prompt-injection attacks, including a timing bypass that motivates validating all visible metadata before tool use.

name: CUA-Universe: A Scalable and Dynamic Environment for Hybrid GUI+CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Turns desktop applications into reproducible GUI-and-CLI environments and generates verified hybrid trajectories for agent post-training.

name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.

name: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.

name: HybridCUA: Learning to Orchestrate GUI and CLI for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains computer agents on verified GUI, command-line, and interleaved trajectories to learn when and how to combine interaction modes.

name: CUAWright: A Minimal Unified Interface for Digital Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies a minimal terminal-based execution framework that lets digital agents construct tools and manage context across browser, desktop, and CAD tasks.

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces OpenMobile-2, combining simulated mobile apps, emulator tasks, released training data, and policies that can alternate GUI interaction with app-native tools.

notes: Editorial summary based on the primary paper abstract; experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains native computer-use models to coordinate GUI actions and code execution using hybrid demonstrations and online reinforcement learning.

name: MobileWorld (Tongyi-MAI)
notes: This is Tongyi-MAI/MobileWorld, distinct from jacklishufan/MobileWorld (MobileWorldBench). Public source includes task definitions, verification logic and environment orchestration. The README reports 201 tasks across 20 applications; this is not an independent count of the evolving task tree. Linux/KVM or WSL2/KVM is required by the documented host setup, with macOS support in progress. MCP and simulated-user settings can require separate external services.
summary: A containerized Android evaluation environment with GUI-only, agent-user interaction and MCP-augmented tasks, plus checks on application and backend state.
